subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should a package installation switching to the dev channel ever adopt a pre-existing checkout, or must it create a clean OpenClaw-owned clone and build an explicitly fetched canonical commit?
rationale: Remote URL validation cannot make an attacker-writable Git repository trustworthy because its config, refs, refspecs, objects, and local commits remain authoritative inputs to later Git commands and the build.

options.title: Require a clean clone
options.body: Package-to-dev conversion rejects occupied paths and creates a clean OpenClaw-owned checkout from the canonical repository before building an exact fetched commit.

options.title: Preserve explicit developer adoption
options.body: Keep existing-checkout adoption only as a clearly documented developer opt-in without presenting URL verification as a security boundary, and separately harden the package conversion path.

recommendation.title: Require a clean clone
recommendation.body: Package-to-dev conversion rejects occupied paths and creates a clean OpenClaw-owned checkout from the canonical repository before building an exact fetched commit.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this contributor to the updater's Git execution and command-runner behavior at the center of the decision.
